newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Megawati said facing new questioning.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Megawati said facing new questioning.

text.p: Police will question ousted Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) leader Megawati Sukarnoputri on fresh charges of organising a party function at her home, the Media Indonesia daily said on Friday.
Police were not available for comment.

The paper quoted a police source as saying on Thursday that Megawati would be questioned on charges of organising an illegal meeting after she arranged a function for the party's 24th anniversary at her home last week.
The source said police had sent a letter to President Suharto asking for approval to question Megawati. Such permission is required because she is a member of parliament.
"The letter was officially sent on Wednesday," the source said. The paper gave no other details.
Megawati, ousted by party rebels at a government-sponsored congress last June, held the anniversary function at her south Jakarta residence.
Surjadi, who replaced Megawati at the government-sanctioned congress in June, organised the PDI's official celebration in central Sulawesi.
Megawati said in a strong speech during her function last week that the only legal PDI was the one chaired by her.

Megawati was questioned by the police last year as a witness in connection with riots on July 27 in Jakarta, which were sparked by the police-backed takeover of the party's headquarters by Surjadi's supporters. No charges were ever laid.
At least five people died in the riots, the worst in Jakarta in more than two decades.

Another PDI legislator, Aberson Silaloho will go to trial on Janaury 29 on charges of insulting the president arising from a speech he gave last year as Megawati supporters held on to the PDI's headquarters before their violent eviction.

Megawati last year filed a suit against the government, military and party rivals to have her removal declared illegal. It was dimissed by a lower court which ruled it could not decide on an internal party dispute.
Political analysts said the government supported Megawati's ouster because it feared she was becoming too popular.
The Christian-Nationalist PDI, the ruling Golkar and the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) are the only parties allowed to contest the general elections, scheduled for May 29.
